# Pioneer Estuary {.unnumbered}

*This chapter applies the [budget framework](14-budget-framework.qmd) to the
Pioneer estuary: how the control volume is defined, and what the nitrogen budget
returns for the flood run.*

## The control volume

A budget is computed over a **control volume** (CV) — a contiguous set of mesh
elements whose seaward boundary coincides with the Pioneer Mouth flux transect
and which is otherwise closed by land and the upstream river. For run 003 the CV
is **16,344 elements (4.81 km²)** and contains all three river point sources.

![Pioneer estuary control volume (run 003): the selected CV cells (green fill) drawn on the model mesh, with the mouth `fluxflag` cells (flag-2 blue / flag-3 red outlines), the flag 2↔3 mouth transect (magenta), and the three river inflows (gold). Source: `diagnostics/cv_definition_map.py`.](../../assets/images/budget/cv_definition_map_003.png){#fig-cv-map}

**How the CV is built — three steps, and the files to cross-check or remake it.**
(1) A polygon is drawn around the estuary in lon/lat and saved as
[`cv_pioneer_estuary.csv`](../../../analytics/pioneer_region_flux/configs/cv_pioneer_estuary.csv);
its seaward edge follows the **Pioneer Mouth flag 2↔3 transect** — the line where
`fluxflag.prop` region-2 faces meet region-3 faces — so the CV boundary lands
exactly on the flux-tracked gate. (2) [`build_cv.py`](../../../analytics/nutrient_budget/core/build_cv.py)
reads the mesh (`hgrid.gr3`) and selects every element whose **centroid** falls
inside the polygon (point-in-polygon), writing the 1-indexed element-ID list
[`cv_pioneer_estuary_elements.txt`](../../../analytics/pioneer_region_flux/configs/cv_pioneer_estuary_elements.txt)
— the exact array every budget script integrates over. (3) `cv_definition_map.py`
overlays that element list on the mesh, the `fluxflag.prop` flags and the
`source_sink.in` inflows (@fig-cv-map) so the selection can be verified. To
define a different CV, redraw the polygon CSV and re-run steps 2–3; the inputs
are just `hgrid.gr3`, `cv_pioneer_estuary.csv`, `fluxflag.prop` and
`source_sink.in`.

### The region config (YAML)

The region YAML names the CV element list and the bounding `fluxflag.prop`
regions with their sign conventions
([`configs/pioneer_estuary.yaml`](../../../analytics/pioneer_region_flux/configs/pioneer_estuary.yaml)):

```yaml
name: pioneer_estuary
control_volume_elements: cv_pioneer_estuary_elements.txt
boundary_fluxes:
  - region_id: 3
    sign: +1
    label: "Pioneer Mouth (region 3 -> region 2): positive = bay -> estuary, INTO CV"
integrate_atm_over_cv: true
integrate_swi_over_cv: true
```

### Boundary tracking caveat

A critical subtlety for the boundary term: `flux.out` records transport only
across mesh edges where the two adjacent `fluxflag.prop` values **differ by
exactly 1 and neither is −1**. If part of the CV perimeter is the (−1, region)
interface or a same-flag edge, transport through it is invisible to the budget.
This turns out to be the heart of the Pioneer mouth problem.

## Tracer transport through the control volume

Before quantifying the budget, it helps to see what is being budgeted. The
conservative tracers injected at the river source spread through the estuary and
exchange across the mouth transect — the storage and boundary terms the budget
must capture. The dilute plume is clearest zoomed in on the Pioneer mouth:

{{< video ../../assets/videos/tracer_mouth_zoom.mp4 >}}

*Conservative-tracer plume around the Pioneer mouth (zoomed). Source:
`analytics/animations/animate_trc_zoomed.py`.*

## The Pioneer nitrogen budget

Running the framework over this CV for the 14-day flood window produces the
standard outputs. The stacked-area plot shows the instantaneous balance of
terms; the cumulative plot integrates them to tonnes of nitrogen.

::: {layout-ncol=2}
![Instantaneous mass balance (stacked area). Source: `nutrient_budget/core/report.py`](../../assets/images/budget/budget_stacked.png){#fig-budget-stacked}

![Cumulative time-integrals (tonnes N). Source: `nutrient_budget/core/report.py`](../../assets/images/budget/budget_cumulative.png){#fig-budget-cumulative}
:::

The conservative checks come first. Volume and salinity should close tightly; if
they do not, the nutrient terms cannot be trusted. The conservative tracers
(`GEN_1`, `TRC_tr1`) give a second, source-driven check.

::: {layout-ncol=2}
![Volume and salinity closure. Source: `…/diagnostics/conservation_check.py`](../../assets/images/budget/conservation_VOL_Salinity.png){#fig-cons-volsal}

![Conservative-tracer closure (`GEN_1`, `TRC_tr1`). Source: `…/diagnostics/conservation_check.py`](../../assets/images/budget/conservation_GEN1_TRC_tr1.png){#fig-cons-gen}
:::

A whole-domain balance infers the open-boundary term by difference, providing an
independent view on closure:

![Global mass balance — closing the ocean-boundary term by residual. Source: `…/diagnostics/global_balance.py`](../../assets/images/budget/global_balance.png){#fig-global-balance}

## The budget report

Each run also writes a self-contained **`report.html`** — the plots, the closure
residual, and the sanity commentary in one page. The report below is the 14-day
nitrogen budget for run **002** (`pioneer_N_002_14d`):

```{=html}
<iframe src="../../assets/reports/pioneer_N_002_14d_report.html"
        width="100%" height="600"
        style="border:1px solid #c8cdd2; border-radius:4px;"></iframe>
```

[Open the full report in a new tab →](../../assets/reports/pioneer_N_002_14d_report.html)

::: {.callout-important}
**Read this budget with one caveat.** Run 002 was produced on an earlier build
affected by the *"only NCS_ss1 registers"* output bug, so its combined AED files
contain only the sediment (`NCS_ss1`) diagnostics — **none of the nitrogen rate,
sediment–water or atmospheric diagnostics were saved.** Terms B (internal sinks),
C (atmospheric) and D (sediment–water) are therefore **unavailable and set to
zero**, and the storage term uses a `zCoordinates`-derived layer thickness in
place of `ENV_layer_ht`. The large residual consequently conflates those
genuinely-missing terms with the conservation issues discussed next — it is
**not** a pure closure error. A run on the fixed build that saves the full
diagnostic set is needed for a closeable nitrogen budget.
:::

For this run the residual does **not** close — the storage change far exceeds the
tracked source and boundary terms. The forensic account of the conservation
issues, and how an independent cross-check confirmed them, is the subject of
[Conservation Testing](16-conservation-testing.qmd).
